newsitem.title: USA: Medtronic buys stake in PharmaTarget.
newsitem.headline: Medtronic buys stake in PharmaTarget.

text.p: Medtronic Inc purchased a nine percent stake in PharmaTarget Inc, a privately held company which is developing an implantable device to treat atrial fibrillation (AFib), the companies said on Friday.
Financial terms were not disclosed. The investment gives Medtronic a seat on PharmaTarget's board of directors.

AFib is a condition when both atria, the top chambers of the heart, stop beating regularly and start to quiver. PharmaTarget, a developmental stage company, is developing the Implantable Pharmacologic Atrioverter (IPA) to treat it.
AFib affects more than six million people worldwide. PharmaTarget said nearly $8 billion was spent in 1994 on the treatment of AFib in the United States alone.

PharmaTarget said it expects to have its first working prototype of its IPA at the end of 1998, and expects to introduce the device in Europe in the first half of 1999 and then two or three years later in the United States.
Larry Shearon, vice president of corporate technology for Medtronic, has been appointed to PharmaTarget's board.
"It's a new technology that we feel may have a lot of potential," Shearon said of PharmaTarget's IPA.
The existing standard treatment for AFib is an in-hospital procedure using either electrical shocks or medications, and patients are then put on a life-long drug program.
